Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

rows.explainer:
Assumption For simplicity, we assume the iron content of "over-fortified" rice (i.e. rice fortified above the maximum standard) is the same as the iron content of adequately fortified rice (i.e. rice fortified above the minimum and below the maximum standard).

"The GoI recommends that rice be fortified with between 28 and 42.5 mg of iron per kg of rice with ferric pyrophosphate as source of iron. At this consumption level and with the existing range of iron level in the GoI’s rice fortification standards, both women of reproductive age (WRA) (15 to 49 years old) and adult men will receive between 4.7 to 7.1 mg of iron per day." Nutrition International, "Investigation plan for TA for fortification of rice in India (February 15, 2023), p. 15. https://files.givewell.org/files/Interventions/Nutrition_International/NI_Response_Follow-up_Questions_Rice_fortification_India_2023-03-01.docx

rows.explainer: Assumption We apply a 60% skeptical adjustment because the quality compliance data informing this estimate come from a different state. We expect implementation quality in the modeled states to be somewhat lower, so we reduce the estimated additional iron content by 40% to account for this uncertainty.
